answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, so a seat is cut from hard rock like a mesa, never handed out free. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations, each an island of real cost. The toll climbs with head count like a rising river, so cheap mass registration stalls against compute no shortcut can forge.
